text:
Nikita Kucherov's future in Tampa has been the subject of a week of trade talk, and even Andrei Vasilevskiy has said publicly he hopes the two sides find a "perfect golden middle," as The Athletic's headline put it. On Wednesday in Buffalo, Kucherov answered none of those questions and all of the hockey ones: three goals and an assist in an 8-3 Lightning win.

Tampa Bay owned the first period, 1.95 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 0.76, and scored twice in the last 71 seconds of it. Scott Sabourin finished a 47% chance at 18:49, and John Carlson's power-play snap shot made it 2-0 at 19:38. Brandon Hagel and Yanni Gourde stretched it to 4-0 in the second, Gourde's goal giving 2024 second-round pick Sam O'Reilly, up with Brayden Point on injured reserve, his first NHL point.

Then Buffalo found something. Josh Doan tipped in a power-play goal at 15:54, Jason Zucker scored with 28 seconds left in the second, and Tage Thompson, eyeing the 50-goal mark according to Buffalo Hockey Beat, hammered a slap shot 33 seconds into the third that had a 2% chance of going in. It was 4-3, and the Sabres had a 27% chance. It lasted 52 seconds. Kucherov scored on a backhand at 1:25, again at 4:11 and on the power play at 14:13, and Hagel added an eighth. Carlson finished with a goal and four assists, passing 800 career points; Jake Guentzel had four assists.

The scoreboard says rout. The chances don't: 3.44 expected goals for Tampa Bay, 3.37 for Buffalo, and Buffalo out-attempted the Lightning 61-34. Our deserved-to-win measure (the share of replays of every shot a team wins) had it at 52% to 48%. The gap was in net. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen allowed five on 14 shots, 2.3 goals worse than those shots deserved, and Colten Ellis allowed three on eight in relief. Vasilevskiy stopped 28 of 31, a little better than expected.

Buffalo can take something from the push back from 4-0, and very little else. Tampa leaves with a hat trick from the player everyone is talking about, which will only make the talking louder.
headline: Kucherov's hat trick buries the Sabres
